Architecture: Kubernetes clusters consist of a control plane managing worker nodes. The control plane runs the API server, scheduler, controller manager, and etcd as core components.
Pods: Pods are the smallest deployable units, containing one or more containers with shared storage and network. Each pod gets a unique cluster IP.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:latest
kubectl Basics: kubectl is the CLI for controlling Kubernetes clusters. Common commands manage resources, view logs, exec into containers, and port-forward.

kubectl create deployment myapp --image=nginx
kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl logs pod-name
kubectl exec -it pod-name -- /bin/sh
Namespaces: Namespaces provide virtual cluster isolation for multi-tenant environments. Resources in one namespace are invisible to other namespaces by default.

kubectl create namespace staging
kubectl get pods --namespace=staging
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=staging

Deployments: Deployments manage ReplicaSets and provide declarative updates with rolling updates, rollbacks, and scaling capabilities.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.21
StatefulSets: StatefulSets manage stateful applications with stable network identities, ordered deployment, and persistent storage per pod.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
spec:
  serviceName: "db"
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:13
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
DaemonSets: DaemonSets ensure all or selected nodes run a copy of a pod, ideal for logging, monitoring, and networking agents that run on every node.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fluentd
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: fluentd
        image: fluent/fluentd:v1.16
Jobs & CronJobs: Jobs run a pod to completion, useful for batch processing and migrations. CronJobs run jobs on a recurring schedule using cron syntax.

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: migrate
        image: myapp:latest
        command: ["node", "migrate.js"]
      restartPolicy: Never
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: cleanup
            image: alpine
            command: ["sh", "-c", "find /data -delete"]

ClusterIP: ClusterIP exposes a service on an internal cluster IP accessible only within the cluster. It is the default Service type for internal communication.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nginx
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
NodePort: NodePort exposes a service on each node's IP at a static port, making it accessible externally via nodeIP:nodePort.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
  - port: 80
    nodePort: 30080
LoadBalancer: LoadBalancer provisions an external load balancer from cloud providers and assigns a public IP for internet-facing services.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
Ingress: Ingress exposes HTTP/S routes to services with host/path-based routing, TLS termination, and virtual hosting.

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
spec:
  rules:
  - host: myapp.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: myapp
            port:
              number: 80
Network Policies: Network Policies control traffic flow between pods using label selectors and port rules. By default all pod-to-pod traffic is allowed.

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: frontend
    ports:
    - port: 8080

ConfigMaps: ConfigMaps store non-sensitive configuration data as key-value pairs or files that pods consume as environment variables or volumes.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-config
data:
  APP_ENV: production
  APP_DEBUG: "false"
Secrets: Secrets store sensitive data like passwords and API keys base64-encoded. They are injected into pods as environment variables or mounted volumes.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
type: Opaque
data:
  DB_PASSWORD: cGFzc3dvcmQxMjM=

kubectl create secret generic db-pass --from-literal=password=password123
Environment Variables: Environment variables in pods reference ConfigMaps and Secrets directly or via configMapKeyRef and secretKeyRef selectors.

containers:
- name: app
  env:
  - name: APP_ENV
    valueFrom:
      configMapKeyRef:
        name: app-config
        key: APP_ENV
  - name: DB_PASSWORD
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: db-secret
        key: password
ResourceQuotas: ResourceQuotas limit total resource consumption per namespace, preventing any single team or app from exhausting cluster resources.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "10"
    requests.memory: 20Gi
    limits.cpu: "20"
    limits.memory: 40Gi
    pods: "50"
    persistentvolumeclaims: "10"
LimitRanges: LimitRanges set minimum and maximum resource constraints per pod or container within a namespace, preventing runaway resource usage.

apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: 2Gi
    min:
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: 256Mi
    type: Container

Volumes: Container volumes provide temporary or persistent storage attached to pods. Volume types include emptyDir, hostPath, and cloud disks.

volumes:
- name: data
  emptyDir: {}
containers:
- name: app
  volumeMounts:
  - mountPath: /data
    name: data
PersistentVolumes: PersistentVolumes are cluster-wide storage resources provisioned by administrators or dynamically via StorageClass.

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data
PVCs: PersistentVolumeClaims request storage resources from a PersistentVolume, binding to matching volumes based on capacity and access modes.

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
StorageClass: StorageClass provisions PersistentVolumes dynamically based on cloud provider storage types like SSD, HDD, or custom parameters.

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
provisioner: kubernetes.io/gce-pd
parameters:
  type: pd-ssd

HPA: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler automatically scales pod replicas based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics from Prometheus.

apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: web
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: requests_per_second
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: 1000
VPA: Vertical Pod Autoscaler adjusts CPU and memory requests for pods based on actual usage, improving resource efficiency.

apiVersion: autoscaling.k8s.io/v1
kind: VerticalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  targetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: app
  updatePolicy:
    updateMode: Auto
  resourcePolicy:
    containerPolicies:
    - containerName: '*'
      minAllowed:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 256Mi
      maxAllowed:
        cpu: "4"
        memory: 8Gi
Cluster Autoscaler: Cluster Autoscaler automatically adds or removes nodes in a cloud provider's node group based on pending pod resource requests.

# Cluster Autoscaler scales the node group when pods can't be scheduled
# AWS: deploy to EKS with IAM role
# GCP: enable node auto-provisioning
# Azure: enable cluster autoscaler in AKS

kubectl get nodes # Check current nodes

Helm Basics: Helm is the Kubernetes package manager. Charts package YAML templates into reusable, configurable releases with versioning.

helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
helm install my-release bitnami/nginx
helm list
helm uninstall my-release
Chart Structure: Helm charts follow a standard directory structure. Values.yaml provides defaults, and templates use Go templating for dynamic resource generation.

mychart/
  Chart.yaml          # Metadata: name, version, description
  values.yaml         # Default configuration values
  templates/          # Go template YAML files
    deployment.yaml
    service.yaml
    _helpers.tpl       # Named templates (partials)
  charts/             # Subchart dependencies
  crds/               # Custom Resource Definitions
Values & Templates: Helm templates use Go template syntax with Sprig functions. Values are injected from values.yaml or --set CLI flags.

# templates/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        resources:
          {{- toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 10 }}
Helm Hooks: Hooks run actions at specific points in a release lifecycle: pre/post install, upgrade, delete. Useful for database migrations and validation.

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  annotations:
    helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade
    helm.sh/hook-weight: "-5"
    helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: hook-succeeded
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: migrate
        image: myapp:latest
        command: ["node", "migrate.js"]

CRDs: Custom Resource Definitions extend the Kubernetes API with custom resources that behave like built-in objects.

apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: Database
    plural: databases
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              engine:
                type: string
              version:
                type: string
Operators: Operators automate application management by extending Kubernetes with custom controllers. They watch CRD resources and reconcile desired state.
Service Mesh: Service meshes like Istio provide traffic management, security, and observability for microservices. They use sidecar proxies to intercept network traffic.

# Istio features:
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
spec:
  hosts:
  - myapp
  http:
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: /v2
    route:
    - destination:
        host: myapp-v2
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: myapp-v1

# Traffic splitting (canary)
kind: DestinationRule
spec:
  subsets:
  - name: v1
    labels:
      version: v1
  - name: v2
    labels:
      version: v2

RBAC: Role-Based Access Control restricts API access via Roles (namespace-scoped) and ClusterRoles (cluster-scoped) bound to users or ServiceAccounts.

apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
ServiceAccounts: ServiceAccounts provide identities for pods to authenticate with the Kubernetes API, used with RBAC for fine-grained permissions.

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: my-app-sa
---
# Pod using the SA
spec:
  serviceAccountName: my-app-sa
Pod Security: Pod Security Standards (restricted, baseline, privileged) enforce security contexts at the namespace level, preventing privileged containers.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: baseline
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: baseline

Metrics Server: Metrics Server collects resource utilization data from kubelet and exposes it via the Metrics API, enabling kubectl top and HPA.
Prometheus: Prometheus monitors Kubernetes with time-series metrics collection, alerting, and Grafana dashboards for visualization.

helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts
helm install prometheus prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack
Logging: Logging in Kubernetes uses fluentd or Loki to collect container logs and forward them to Elasticsearch, Loki, or cloud logging services.

# View logs
kubectl logs -l app=myapp --tail=100
kubectl logs pod-name --previous

# Structured logging
# Use JSON log format in applications
# Deploy fluent-bit DaemonSet to collect logs
# Send to Elasticsearch or Loki
